posts.title: What the numbers cannot hold
posts.hook: I left a session last week with that familiar weight in my chest.
posts.caption:
I left a session last week with that familiar weight in my chest.

Not because the leader was failing. Because what he was carrying would never show up in a product dashboard: incomplete information, a team frozen in a way no curriculum names cleanly, a life question dressed up as a performance problem. We did real work. None of it would compress into an interaction count.

Then I went home and read the capital story. ADP Ventures into Valence. Conversation volume starting to look like a product metric. That layer is real. Fluency at scale is a real job. I respect it.

I used to feel pressure to pick a tribe, scale story or depth story. I don't anymore. Different jobs. I choose the hours where complexity is the brief, not the obstacle.

If you buy or lead above the director line, fund the layer that matches the weight you are actually carrying.

#executivecoaching #leadershipdevelopment #peoplestrategy

posts.title: Green boxes, dirty problem
posts.hook: A leader came in with a clean deck and a dirty problem.
posts.caption:
A leader came in with a clean deck and a dirty problem.

Every box on the transformation plan was green. Sponsors were getting updates. The team was "aligned" in every forum that required a slide. Nothing that mattered was actually moving. You could feel the air in the room get careful when we got near the real issue.

We didn't fix the deck. We sat with the sentence he had been avoiding: he was performing progress for the system, because real progress would force a conflict he did not want to own yet.

Once that was named, the work got simpler and harder at the same time. The next move was one hard conversation he had been protecting people from having.

I read a lot about content, modules, and AI practice reps right now. Some of that is useful.

What I care about when I close the laptop after a session is narrower: did we produce movement, or evidence of movement?

Those are not the same craft.

#executivecoaching #leadership #changemanagement

posts.title: Work that holds on Friday afternoon
posts.hook: When I was leading teams inside Fortune 500 transformations, the plan was rarely what kept me up.
posts.caption:
When I was leading teams inside Fortune 500 transformations, the plan was rarely what kept me up.

What kept me up was whether the work would hold when a real customer, peer, or sponsor pushed back on a Friday afternoon. Pretty problem statements died in those rooms. So did clever frameworks that looked sharp on Tuesday and folded by week's end.

I still coach for that test.

In the room now I am less interested in whether the language sounds sharp and more interested in whether the decision still stands when someone important pushes. Gut still has a job when the playbook stops matching the people in front of me.

Home taught me the same thing quieter. Attention is finite. If I give the polished version of myself to work and the leftovers to the people I love, both places feel it.

I don't coach the title. I coach the whole person who showed up, because that is who has to execute when the room gets sharp.

#leadership #executivecoaching #wholeperson

posts.title: Package altitude is the first sale
posts.hook: I watched a serious buyer light up over a syllabus before anyone named what they were actually buying.
posts.caption:
I watched a serious buyer light up over a syllabus before anyone named what they were actually buying.

Faculty name. Brand heat. Energy in the room went up. Six months later the sponsor could not defend the spend, because package altitude never got locked. Seats, academy pathway, private cohort, full custom: those are different buys with different success dashboards.

I keep relearning this the hard way in design rooms. Start with business priority (profit, cost, or risk), then what leaders must do differently, then metrics, then design. Start with a wish list and "we need a leadership program" and you often buy recognition. That can be valid. It is not the same purchase as transformation.

I sit closer to private-cohort and high-stakes human work on purpose: intact teams, sponsor-tied application, rooms where judgment under pressure is the constraint, not seat count.

Name the package before you fall in love with the syllabus.

#leadershipdevelopment #executiveeducation #peoplestrategy

posts.title: Not only her capability
posts.hook: A company sent me a high-performing director and called it a leadership problem.
posts.caption:
A company sent me a high-performing director and called it a leadership problem.

She was sharp. Willing. Already carrying more than her title suggested. By session two I could feel it in my gut: the bottleneck was not her capability. It was a leadership team that could not make a clean decision without reopening it three forums later. She was being asked to outrun a rhythm nobody wanted to name.

We still did the individual work: identity, presence, how she was landing. We also put the system on the table, quietly, without turning the coaching into a blame session.

Individual certificates without team-level change are a common buy. Sometimes they help. Often they become a private gym membership next to a broken operating rhythm.

I care about the person in the chair. I also care whether the intact team can execute after the insight lands. Otherwise we did theater with better language.

If you sponsor development, ask what has to change in the room around them, not only in them.

#teamcoaching #executivecoaching #leadership

posts.title: Stress as climate
posts.caption:
Here's something I wrestle with.

The field keeps publishing what a lot of us already feel in our bodies: leaders under rising stress, thin bench confidence, cost pressure sitting next to readiness goals. I don't doubt the numbers. I doubt our response.

More content is the easy answer. More AI practice is the fashionable one. Both can help at the right layer. Neither automatically builds a leader who can stay human while the system tightens.

What I trust more, slowly, is a relationship dense enough for the real sentence under the performance narrative. Why a capable person goes still, or leaves, or performs green while the work dies. I have sat across from that sentence enough times to know it does not arrive on a content calendar.

I do not have a clean package name for that. I have a choice about where I put my hours.

I am still building what works when the stress is not a quarter, but a climate.

#leadership #executivecoaching #peoplestrategy

posts.title: Where the agenda actually lives
posts.hook: I do not learn the CHRO agenda from a slide first.
posts.caption:
I do not learn the CHRO agenda from a slide first.

I learn it when a people leader is trying to fund readiness while the enterprise is still optimizing cost, and the room goes quiet around what will actually get sponsored. Leader development still wins airtime. Change and resiliency climbed. Tech and AI stopped being side hobbies. Engagement, as the lead frame, lost altitude. That map only matters if you can feel where money and attention already go.

I work where those investments get messy: leaders and intact teams who need movement, not theater. Applied work under real load, not a content library.

Over 1,500 hours with 250+ senior leaders and founders, globally, has not made me romantic about any of this. It has made me practical about what holds when a customer, peer, or sponsor pushes back.

If you own that agenda, the useful split is still the same. Scale where scale fits. Depth where depth is the actual requirement.

#leadershipdevelopment #executivecoaching #peoplestrategy

posts.title: Wrong layer (quiet door)
posts.hook: The costliest development mistake I see is not hiring the wrong person.
posts.caption:
The costliest development mistake I see is not hiring the wrong person.

It is buying the wrong layer of help for the actual problem.

A manager drowning in new scope often needs structured skill, feedback loops, and practice reps. Scaled support, including AI-assisted practice, can serve that well.

A VP who looks composed in every forum and cannot sleep because the role and the rest of their life are no longer the same person needs something else. I have sat in that quieter room. Relationship sturdy enough for an inconvenient truth. Slower. Not a five-module fix.

I coach that second category on purpose. Whole person. Not title only. Movement after truth.

If you are a senior leader carrying more than your org chart shows, or you sponsor someone who is, you already know which layer you are in.
